propositions: A failed tickets-branch push rejection is not delivered to callers on the async, library, and MCP write paths because stderr/logging handlers are bypassed or inaccessible in those surfaces, leaving the failure invisible even though the CLI/sync path was fixed.

The remedy is a durable marker file recorded in the git dir at the single _raise_if_strict choke point that every push failure already funnels through, exposed via rebar.push_status() for library callers and a push_status field on all MCP write-tool results.

The async path (detached Popen with stderr=DEVNULL) now records the marker durationally so a later read detects the failure despite the child's stderr being discarded; tests poll the marker on a 60s bounded deadline.

The library path (in-process rebar.comment) now returns push status via rebar.push_status() without requiring a logging handler, and the MCP path returns push_status alongside result in write-tool outputs so agents can read it from the tool result.

Non-push-attempted reasons (push-disabled, remote-not-found, invalid-destination, async-delivery-unobservable) are not recorded to avoid false pending status on local-only stores; all other failures including commit-phase and recovery reasons are recorded to make invisible failures visible.

The marker is structural, lives in the git dir (not the working tree), has no .json suffix, clears on successful push, and is best-effort so marker write failures do not fail the write; the default contract that push_tickets_branch always returns None and never raises is preserved.
